item.title: IDF warns of rising Iranian missile fire as Trump's deadline nears
item.description:
The Israel Defense Forces warned late Tuesday that missile fire toward Israeli territory could intensify "in the coming hours" as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached with no deal in sight.

In a statement, the IDF urged the public to "remain vigilant, alert, and act responsibly, while continuing to follow the Home Front Command's instructions". The warning came as Iran fired fresh salvos of ballistic missiles at central and southern Israel on Tuesday, with cluster munitions striking multiple locations in the Sharon plain, according to the IDF. Earlier in the day, the military had urged Iranians to avoid train travel nationwide, before confirming strikes on a railway bridge in Kashan that killed at least two people.

item.title: Iranians form human chains at power plants as energy strikes loom
item.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached on Tuesday, Iranian authorities launched a nationwide campaign calling on young people to form "human chains" around power plants and other critical infrastructure in a bid to deter threatened American strikes.

item.title: Iranians form human chains around power plants as energy strikes loom
item.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached on Tuesday, Iranian authorities launched a nationwide campaign calling on young people to form "human chains" around the country's power plants and energy infrastructure in a dramatic act of defiance.

item.title: US, Israel strike Iran's largest aluminum plant
item.description: American and Israeli forces struck the Iran Aluminium Company (IRALCO) in Arak on Tuesday, targeting the country's largest aluminum producer and sparking a major fire at the facility, as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz drew near. The strike marks a further expansion of the five-week US-Israeli air campaign into Iran's core industrial base, following earlier attacks on steel mills, petrochemical complexes, and nuclear sites.

item.title: Iran fires cluster munitions at central Israel as war enters sixth week
item.description: Iran launched multiple ballistic missile barrages targeting Israeli cities on Tuesday, with cluster munitions striking areas across central Israel and causing widespread property damage, though Israeli emergency services reported no fatalities from the day's attacks.

item.title: Trump confirms 'heated negotiations' as Iran deadline nears
item.description:
With hours remaining before President Trump's self-imposed 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, the president confirmed that the United States was engaged in active talks with Tehran but refused to share details. "We're in heated negotiations," Trump told Fox News in a phone call, declining to say how he felt about the discussions.

The disclosure came as Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif made a last-ditch appeal for more time, posting on X that he "earnestly" requested Trump extend his deadline by two weeks. Sharif asked Iran to reopen the strait during that same period "as a goodwill gesture" and called on "all warring parties to observe a ceasefire everywhere for two weeks to allow diplomacy to achieve conclusive termination of war." White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Trump "has been made aware of the proposal, and a response will come," according to CBS News and ABC News. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran was "positively reviewing" the Pakistani proposal.

item.title: Trump agrees to two-week Iran ceasefire hours before strike deadline
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday evening that he would suspend planned military strikes against Iran for two weeks, calling the arrangement a "double-sided ceasefire" just hours after warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if no deal was reached by his 8 p.m. ET deadline. The pause is conditional on Iran agreeing to the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the Strait of Hormuz, with Trump citing a 10-point proposal from Tehran as a "workable basis" for negotiations toward a longer-term peace agreement.

The announcement followed a last-minute diplomatic push by Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who publicly urged Trump on X to extend his deadline by two weeks "to allow diplomacy to run its course". Sharif also called on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz during the same period "as a goodwill gesture". Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir, whom Trump has previously called his "favourite" field marshal, had been in communication overnight with U.S. Vice President JD Vance and special envoy Steve Witkoff, as well as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

item.title: Trump suspends Iran strikes for two weeks, citing progress on peace deal
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday evening that he would suspend U.S. military strikes on Iran for two weeks, pulling back from his threat to destroy the country's power plants and bridges just 88 minutes before his self-imposed 8 p.m. ET deadline. The announcement, posted on Truth Social at 6:32 p.m. ET, came after a day in which Trump had warned that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Iran did not agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

"Based on conversations with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, of Pakistan, and wherein they requested that I hold off the destructive force being sent tonight to Iran, and subject to the Islamic Republic of Iran agreeing to the COMPLETE, IMMEDIATE, and SAFE OPENING of the Strait of Hormuz, I agree to suspend the bombing and attack of Iran for a period of two weeks," Trump wrote.

item.title: Iran accepts two-week ceasefire hours before Trump's deadline to strike
item.description:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council on Tuesday confirmed it had accepted a two-week ceasefire in its war with the United States, the Associated Press reported, pulling the two nations back from the brink of a catastrophic escalation just hours after President Donald Trump warned that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Tehran did not capitulate to his demands.

The announcement came shortly before Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline expired, capping a day of extreme brinkmanship in which U.S. forces struck military targets on Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub and Israeli warplanes hit bridges and railway infrastructure across the country.

item.title: Afghanistan calls China-brokered talks with Pakistan 'useful'
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban-led government on Tuesday described ongoing peace talks with Pakistan in China as "useful," even as Pakistan's military chief vowed to press forward with military operations against militant targets on Afghan soil, underscoring the fragility of the diplomatic effort.

item.title: Oil prices drop as Pakistan-brokered ceasefire pauses US-Iran strikes
item.description: Six weeks of war between the United States and Iran have sent oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel, fueling the sharpest inflation fears since 2023 and forcing the Federal Reserve into a holding pattern on interest rates. On Tuesday, a last-minute two-week ceasefire brokered by Pakistan offered a glimmer of relief — crude prices dropped sharply in evening trading — but economists warn the damage to consumer confidence and the inflation outlook may already be done.

item.title: Dated Brent surges to record $144 as Iran war chokes supply
item.description:
Physical oil prices hit an all-time high on Tuesday as the war in Iran, now in its sixth week, continues to choke global crude supply through the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Dated Brent, the benchmark for North Sea crude bought and sold for near-term delivery, soared above $144 a barrel — the highest level since the pricing series began in 1987, according to Bloomberg.

The record in physical prices underscores the growing desperation among refiners scrambling to secure barrels for immediate delivery, even as Brent futures for June settled lower near $109 a barrel on Tuesday. The widening gap between spot and futures prices reflects a market where traders are paying steep premiums for crude they can get their hands on now.

item.title: US and Iran set for pivotal peace talks Friday in Islamabad
item.description:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirmed that formal negotiations with the United States will begin on Friday, April 10, in Islamabad, following a dramatic two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump on Tuesday evening just 90 minutes before his own deadline to launch devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

The SNSC, in a statement posted to its Telegram channel, said Iran would enter the talks with "complete distrust of the American side" and stressed that agreeing to negotiate "does not mean the end of the war". Iran has allocated up to two weeks for the negotiations, with the possibility of extension by mutual agreement.

item.title: Physical crude hits all-time high as Hormuz crisis deepens
item.description:
The price of physical crude oil surged to all-time highs on Tuesday, with some grades nearing $150 a barrel as European and Asian refiners scrambled for immediate supply, underscoring the severity of the energy crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

Dated Brent, the benchmark used to price much of the world's physical crude, reached a record $144.42 per barrel on Tuesday afternoon, surpassing levels seen during both the 2008 financial crisis and Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, according to data compiled by S&P Global Platts. North Sea Forties crude climbed to $146.09 a barrel, also an all-time high, according to LSEG data. When the Platts dated Brent assessment is used as a base, many physical cargoes effectively priced above $150 a barrel.

item.title: North Korea fires projectile a day after rare diplomatic thaw
item.description:
North Korea launched an unidentified projectile from its capital area on Tuesday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed on Wednesday, in a move that came just one day after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret over drone incursions into the North.

The JCS said it detected the launch from the Pyongyang region and that South Korean and U.S. intelligence authorities are analyzing the projectile, without providing further details. The projectile, believed to have been fired in the morning, apparently failed shortly after launch, according to the Korea Times, citing Yonhap.

item.title: Physical crude prices top 2008 records as Hormuz blockade deepens
item.description: European and Asian refiners are paying record prices of nearly $150 a barrel for physical crude oil cargoes, surpassing levels last seen during the 2008 financial crisis, as Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues to choke global supply.

item.title: Israel backs US-Iran ceasefire but excludes Lebanon fight
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu endorsed President Donald Trump's decision to suspend airstrikes on Iran for two weeks, but made clear that the deal does not extend to Israel's military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, setting up a potential fault line in the fragile truce before negotiations have even begun.

The announcement came on Tuesday after Trump pulled back from his threat to destroy Iran's bridges, power plants, and civilian infrastructure, declaring a mutual ceasefire contingent on Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Israel agreed to the terms of the two-week ceasefire, according to the Associated Press, citing a White House official. But Netanyahu's office stressed that the agreement applies only to the Iran front — not to Lebanon, where Israeli forces have been conducting a grinding campaign against the Iranian-backed militant group since early March.

item.title: China helped push Iran to accept ceasefire, AP reports
item.description:
Hours before President Donald Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz expired on Tuesday, a two-week ceasefire was announced — and behind the scenes, China appears to have played a quiet but critical role in getting Tehran to the table.

According to the Associated Press, Chinese officials were in direct contact with their Iranian counterparts as ceasefire negotiations evolved, encouraging Tehran to find a path toward a deal. The New York Times reported that Iran faced pressure from China to accept Pakistan's two-week truce proposal, while the New York Post, citing Iranian officials, said China joined Pakistan in urging Iran to agree.

item.title: Amsterdam researchers build metamaterials that learn to change shape
item.description: Researchers at the University of Amsterdam have built synthetic materials that can learn to change shape, adapt their behavior, and move on their own — all without any central control system. The work, published on Monday in Nature Physics, blurs the line between engineered objects and living systems.

item.title: Oil plunges, stock futures surge after U.S.-Iran ceasefire
item.description: Oil prices plummeted below $100 a barrel and U.S. stock futures jumped on Tuesday evening after President Donald Trump announced a two-week ceasefire with Iran, pulling back from an 8 p.m. ET deadline that had threatened the destruction of Iranian civilian infrastructure. The announcement, made on Truth Social around 6:30 p.m. ET, marked a dramatic reversal from hours of escalating threats that had rattled global markets throughout the day.
